pairs.question: Vultis scire, quare patrem non relinquam?
pairs.answer: Quia genuit me, quia educavit, quia abdicavit.
pairs.derivation: Self-posed rhetorical question fully answered by the same speaker. Question is the interrogative 'Vultis scire, quare patrem non relinquam?'; answer is the contiguous tricolon to the first full stop. Stops before 'Diu dubitavi...', which begins a new thought. No words altered; question mark already present, terminal period normalized on the answer.

pairs.question: Merito abdicasti an immerito?
pairs.answer: Si immerito abdicasti, odi patrem tot eicientem innocentes; si merito, odi domum tot facientem nocentes.
pairs.derivation: Genuine alternative question ('rightly or wrongly?') answered by the speaker's own symmetric two-part conditional. Answer ends at the full stop before 'Aliquid in domo locupleti...'. Verbatim and contiguous; no ellipsis.

pairs.question: Quare recusas?
pairs.answer: Ne auferam patri filium, filiis patrem.
pairs.derivation: Source: "'Quare (recusas?)' respondeo: ne auferam patri filium, filiis patrem." The framing verb 'respondeo' is dropped as narration of the reply. Editorial supplement parentheses around 'recusas' stripped, word kept. The quoted question 'Quare recusas?' is genuinely answered by the contiguous clause; capitalization and terminal period normalized.

pairs.question: Quaeris, quod ius iurandum fuerit?
pairs.derivation: Self-posed question ('You ask what the oath was?') answered by the quoted oath formula 'ita patri placeam'. The interrogative 'Quaeris...?' is the question; the answer is the quoted oath, capitalization and terminal period normalized. End of the entry, nothing cut after.

pairs.question: Quod habuisse nos ius iurandum putas?
pairs.answer: Tu nobis religiosum nomen fuisti: si mentiremur, illa sibi iratum patrem invocavit, ego socerum.
pairs.derivation: Self-posed question ('What oath do you think we had?') answered by the speaker. Answer runs to the first full stop, before 'parce, pater: non peieravimus.', which turns to a fresh plea. The interior colon is not a sentence boundary, so the whole sentence is kept contiguous. Capitalization normalized on the answer; question mark already present.
